source.excerpt: The mystery of life is not a problem to be solved;
trail: Wikiquote’s Misattributed section distinguishes a 1982 discussion of Merton from a direct quotation, and cites an exact Merton attribution in a 1998 book. These are its located examples, not an exhaustive chronology.

Two inspected transcriptions of Van der Leeuw’s chapter contain the earlier formulation about reality to be experienced. They do not establish who first created every later “mystery to be lived” variant.

author.heading: About J. J. van der Leeuw
author.bio: J. J. van der Leeuw (1893–1934) was a Dutch theosophist and author. The Conquest of Illusion (1928) develops his account of knowledge through experience; his other work addressed education and the relationship between spiritual realization and institutions.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In The Conquest of Illusion, Van der Leeuw argues that philosophy must draw on experience rather than merely arrange life into intellectual systems. The earlier sentence belongs to a section called “The Mystery of Life.” Its contrast between solving and experiencing helps explain why later versions readily circulated under spiritual writers’ names.
